quote:
This creates the risk of parallel proceedings in two jurisdictions and complicates any negotiation with Velloran.

**Recommended Fix:**
- When requesting Velloran's consent, be prepared for Velloran to assert that any dispute about the consent or its conditions is subject to New York law (if tied to the Side Letter) or Delaware law (if tied to the Distribution Agreement).
- If a consent negotiation breaks down, assess which forum is more favorable and whether the issues can be framed to fit within a single jurisdiction.
reason: The memo correctly identifies the conflict between Side Letter §6 (New York law and New York County courts) and Distribution Agreement §§18.1/18.2 (Delaware law and Wilmington courts). It also cites the §19.4 precedence clause and explains the risk of parallel proceedings. It does not recommend conforming the Side Letter to Delaware. Its fix only says to prepare for forum arguments and pick the more favorable forum if a dispute arises. The criterion explicitly requires that recommendation, so the memo fails.
